## 🔴 Errors (will cause build failures or incorrect behavior)

### 1. `Directory.Build.props`, line 10 — `$(TargetFramework)` condition in `.props` is dead code (AP-21)

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** For single-targeting projects (all projects in this repo), `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation. The SDK's outer build sets `$(TargetFrameworks)` → dispatches inner builds that set `$(TargetFramework)`, but `.props` is imported *before* that dispatch. This condition never matches, so `GenerateDocumentationFile` is **never set to `true`** for any project.

**Fix:** Move this property group to `Directory.Build.targets`, which is imported *after* the SDK sets `$(TargetFramework)`:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets`, lines 6–10 — Property defaults in `.targets` silently override project-level settings

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  <Authors>Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright>Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `.targets` files are imported *after* the project file. MSBuild uses last-write-wins semantics, so these **unconditional** assignments stomp any project-level overrides. Specifically, `LibB.csproj` (line 13) sets `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>`, but this `.targets` file overrides it back to `true` — a silent, confusing bug.

**Fix:** Move these to `Directory.Build.props` with conditional defaults so projects can override:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  <Authors Condition="'$(Authors)' == ''">Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright Condition="'$(Copyright)' == ''">Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 3. `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 13 — Unquoted condition on `$(Configuration)`

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

**Problem:** Missing quotes around both sides. If `$(Configuration)` is empty (e.g., during evaluation or restore), this evaluates as ` == Debug` which is a malformed expression and can produce an MSBuild evaluation error. Even when it doesn't error, it's technically incorrect for values with spaces.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

---

### 4. `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 14 — `DefineConstants` overwrites SDK defaults

```xml
<DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

**Problem:** This **replaces** all existing constants (`DEBUG`, `TRACE`) set by the SDK. Code guarded by `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will silently stop working in Debug configuration.

**Fix:** Append to the existing value:
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 5. `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 43–45 — Publish-on-build re-invokes project via `<MSBuild>` task

```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```

**Problem:** This forks a **second project evaluation** with an additional global property (`_IsPublishing=true`). The second instance shares the same `OutputPath`/`IntermediateOutputPath`, so the two instances race writing the same files. This causes intermittent build failures, especially under parallel builds (`-m`), and doubles the build time for this project.

**Fix:** Use `DependsOnTargets` or `AfterTargets` within the same project instance, with a guard property:
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(PublishAfterBuild)' == 'true'">
  <BuildDependsOn>$(BuildDependsOn);Publish</BuildDependsOn>
</PropertyGroup>
```

### 6. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj`, lines 7–9 — F# compilation order is wrong

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

**Problem:** F# requires files in dependency order. `Services.fs` does `open BrokenOrder.Domain` (depends on `Domain.fs`), but `Services.fs` is listed **before** `Domain.fs`. This will cause a compilation error: the `BrokenOrder.Domain` module is not defined when the compiler processes `Services.fs`.

```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>
